title: Non-system PowerShell and WinRM host processes opened lsass.exe with full/VM-read access on scranton and nashua
summary: On SCRANTON.dmevals.local the hidden loader PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, user pbeesly) opened C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff at 2020-05-02T03:05:16Z (Sysmon EID 10; Security 4656 AccessMask 0x1fffff/0x1f3fff; 4663 AccessMask 0x10 = PROCESS_VM_READ). The same pattern repeats on NASHUA.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:09:29Z from wsmprovhost.exe (WinRM remote PowerShell shell) as user pbeesly with AccessMask 0x1f3fff. Elsewhere in the same window lsass handles are only held by system/AV processes (wininit.exe, csrss.exe, svchost.exe 0x1000/0x101001, MsMpEng.exe, CollectGuestLogs.exe), so these two pbeesly handles stand out as lsass memory access used to read credential material.

title: Attacker script exported LocalMachine certificate private keys to .pfx files, then archived and exfiltrated the collection
summary: On SCRANTON.dmevals.local user pbeesly loaded C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1 which defines Get-PrivateKeys: it enumerates cert:\LocalMachine, exports every certificate with a thumbprint to $env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<random>.pfx protected with the hardcoded password "saribas", and writes the keys to disk (Sysmon EID 11 created C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\coyn5igj.3io.pfx at 03:04:57Z). The staged private keys were then compressed by psversion.ps1's Invoke-Exfil (Compress-7Zip of the whole Downloads dir into %APPDATA%\OfficeSupplies.7z, created 03:08:35Z) and the archive copied to \\192.168.0.4\webdav before Invoke-BeachCleanup deleted the .pfx/.bmp/.png/.7z artifacts.

title: Get-Keystrokes keylogger executed in the pbeesly PowerShell session on scranton
summary: At 2020-05-02T03:06:59Z on SCRANTON.dmevals.local PowerShell PID 3852 (user pbeesly) executed Get-Keystrokes followed by View-Job -JobName "Keystrokes", and at 03:06:47Z the same session ran Keystroke-Check, which enumerates running AV/security products (avp, acs, AvastSvc, nod32krn, ekern ...) before capturing input. The captured keystrokes are a credential-capture primitive used alongside the lsass access in the same session.

title: Clipboard harvested in the same compromised PowerShell session
summary: At 2020-05-02T03:06:42Z on SCRANTON.dmevals.local PowerShell PID 3852 (user pbeesly) ran Get-Clipboard, collecting clipboard contents (frequently passwords) as part of the same credential-collection script set that performed the lsass access and private-key export.

title: Cleartext domain credentials for dmevals\pbeesly passed on a command line to PsExec for lateral movement
summary: On SCRANTON.dmevals.local, from the cwd C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite, the pbeesly PowerShell session repeatedly ran PsExec64.exe against \\NASHUA with the cleartext password for dmevals\pbeesly on the command line ("-u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by -i 2 C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe"), first at 03:11:18Z and again at 03:12:25Z, 03:13:28Z and 03:14:42Z. The credential material is exposed in process command lines/logs and was reused to run the dropped implant C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on nashua under PSEXESVC.
